selected_approach.decision: Preserve host-neutral pure compute/validation modules and same-build Rust traits. Supply scoped host ports only where the actual consumer needs a host capability. Domain types, validation and math must remain usable in another host without Handshake catalog, DB, scheduler or document ownership.

Research-selected portable extension boundary is a versioned WIT world implemented through Wasmtime Component Model, with explicit resource ownership, typed errors and a closed import set. This is a proposed adapter and validation target, not an already implemented host. Preserve PhotoCraft/EffectCraft core-Wasm v1 through explicit legacy adapters; neither source implements Component Model.

Native CLAP and VST3 use their specified native ABI and lifecycle in a separate audio domain adapter. ScorePlugin is the operator-specified domain adapter, not the owner of a second platform catalog/library/permission/scheduler/DB. No existing literal ScorePlugin implementation was established by source search.

Handshake-wide existing logical owners remain behind ports: ResourceBroker authorization/reservations, JobRuntime scheduling, EventLedger receipts/transaction integration and Argus diagnostics. Where an executable shared plugin catalog, library, installation or grant interface is absent from inspected product source, mark a planned gap; do not pretend a new implementation already exists or duplicate an owner.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.finding: SoundCraft reaches native CLAP state save from the device callback. playback drain handles CaptureStates, fill invokes drain and CPAL invokes fill; mix capture_states calls plugin save_state, CLAP delegates to the native state extension. CLAP1.2.7 specifies save/load on the main thread. This is a source-visible thread-contract mismatch; no observed runtime crash is claimed.
INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.control: Implement adapter-owned main/control-thread lifecycle and state lane with bounded commands and explicit acknowledgement. Coordinate audio stop/quiescence before unsafe transitions; keep state blobs, allocation, foreign UI/state calls and persistence outside the callback. Thread affinity is not satisfied by arbitrary spawn_blocking.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.finding: Native plugin loading and processing execute arbitrary foreign code through dynamic libraries and unsafe FFI. A Wasm sandbox or catch_unwind does not contain native memory corruption, aborts or hangs, and scanning/loading itself can execute code.
INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.control: For untrusted native plugins propose a product-managed isolated scanner/worker with OS restrictions, bounded memory/CPU/state/IPC, heartbeat and crash quarantine. The audio bridge requires ahead-of-time prepared fixed buffers, explicit deadline bypass and stable output policy. Measure IPC latency before choosing isolation granularity. No mandatory manually launched external app or daemon is implied.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.finding: EffectCraft limits guest memory to1GiB per instance and fuel per render but its Mutex<Vec<Inst>> pool instantiates on empty and retains successful instances without a global count/byte cap. Concurrent callers can grow the high-water pool; per-instance limits do not bound aggregate resident memory or host scratch copies.
INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.control: Bound active plus idle instances, linear memory, compiled artifact memory and host scratch/result/state bytes per principal/document and globally. Acquire existing ResourceBroker permits before decode/compile/instantiate/copy; retain permits through queued, active and retiring lifetime, release once after confirmed teardown. Pool count and allocator limits must compose with scheduler admission.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.finding: EffectCraft returns the same guest instance to a pool after success. Guest memory/state persists, while the EffectPlugin documentation requires deterministic results and allows parallel rendering. The inspected pool does not reset guest state or bind it to an account/document/revision. PhotoCraft registry is process-global and replaces by plugin id; EffectCraft also uses global registration slots. Cross-principal reuse or id shadowing is an adoption risk, not a proven leak.
INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.control: Key immutable artifacts by verified content hash/API version; use account-scoped catalog grants. Bind instance pools to principal/resource/artifact/state version, reset or discard before reuse across trust scopes, and explicitly model any legitimate persistent domain state. Compare fresh-instance output with reordered pooled invocations using an independent replay oracle.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.finding: VST3 capture replaces controller getState failure with an empty default; restore checks component setState but ignores controller setComponentState/setState results and returns success. Sound mix capture omits unavailable states. Required plugin state can therefore be partial without an equivalent typed partial-success document contract.
INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.control: Return per-instance/per-phase typed outcomes, preserve prior required state on capture failure, and reject a save/restore that claims completeness when required state is absent or refused. Validate state version, artifact identity and total aggregate blob size; perform migration/restore before accepted document commit. Explicit optional-state policy must not silently convert failure into success.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.finding: PhotoCraft has module32MiB, memory512MiB, band4MiB, fuel and sliced wall-deadline checks with imports denied. These are useful sandbox patterns, but compilation, aggregate concurrent runs, host copies and host calls are distinct budgets. EffectCraft fuel alone provides no equivalent wall-deadline control in the inspected render path.
INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.control: Apply bounded compilation admission, fuel/epoch cancellation for guest execution, independent hostcall deadlines/cancellation and bounded outputs. ResourceLimiter covers selected guest resources, not all embedder memory; shared-memory growth requires separate control and should remain disabled until proven. Store lifetime owns instances; retiring stores and host allocations remain charged until reclaimed. Arbitrary Wasm is not real-time safe.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.finding: Native Rust ABI is not stable across compiler versions. EffectCraft's same-build EffectPlugin trait is a useful internal abstraction but does not establish a safe dynamic Rust trait-object plugin ABI. WIT defines a language-neutral interface and resource ownership, not capability policy, determinism or realtime guarantees.
INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.control: Use Rust traits only within the compatible build boundary; choose versioned WIT or the explicitly specified CLAP/VST3 ABI for independent artifacts. Manifest records adapter/world version and schema/state compatibility; incompatible versions fail before execution.

PhotoCraft.api: pc_abi_version, packed manifest pointer/length, pc_alloc and typed filter; imports prohibited
PhotoCraft.lifecycle: compiled Engine/Module shared; fresh Store/Instance for run
PhotoCraft.limits: module32MiB/memory512MiB/band4MiB; one memory, four tables,100000 table elements, one instance, recursion1024; sliced fuel20million; native wall deadline60s
PhotoCraft.error: bounds/type/version/import validation; resumable fuel and abort/deadline; errors captured per operation

EffectCraft.engine: wasmi2.0.0; custom core-Wasm API1; optional wasm feature
EffectCraft.api: ec_api_version, manifest pointer/length, ec_alloc, ec_render; imports prohibited; host frame/parameter copies
EffectCraft.lifecycle: Mutex idle instance pool; repeated successful instance reuse
EffectCraft.limits: memory1GiB/manifest1MiB, one instance per Store; fuelbase50million plus perpixel20000; i32 addressability checked

SoundCraft.api: CLAP and VST3 native ABI via libloading and unsafe foreign calls
SoundCraft.lifecycle: prepare/activate/process/state/control callbacks/deactivate/destroy; thread ownership must follow each native specification
SoundCraft.state_limits: 64MiB native stream guard is not an aggregate session/document cap; VST3 component/controller state phases must retain distinct outcomes

platform_contract_proposals.contract: Platform manifest binds artifact hash, publisher identity supplied by existing account mechanism, adapter/API/world version, compatible domain hosts, declared closed capabilities, inputs/outputs/state schema, resource maxima and lifecycle. Installation/catalog metadata and domain session state are distinct. No shadow DB or platform scheduler in ScorePlugin.

Capability imports use scoped opaque revocable resources, never a raw DB handle, unrestricted filesystem/network or ambient WASI. Declared and granted capabilities must both match; ResourceBroker authorization rechecked at invocation and accepted proposal commit. Imported hostcalls carry cancellation, deadlines, bounded bytes and typed errors; guest cancellation cannot itself preempt an uncooperative hostcall.

Plugin code receives immutable inputs and emits bounded results/proposals. The existing document owner validates principal/resource/content hash/expected revision and accepted mutation plus idempotency/receipt in one transaction. Plugin local KV follows STU-AUT-160 and does not bypass document undo/revision/history. Raw plugin payloads, source paths, buffers and private state must not enter diagnostics by default.

Admission caps slots, bytes, workers, store/instance count and device capacity with fair principal/document allocation. Deadline/cancel lane remains available under saturation. Coalesce only replaceable uncommitted previews; never discard accepted edits or durable exports. Shutdown stops admission, cancels previews, resolves or durably records accepted operations, drains native affinity lanes and releases permits after terminal reclamation.

CLAP/VST lifecycle is a checked state machine with exact main/audio affinity. No compile, dynamic load, state capture/restore, allocation, unbounded command drain, UI calls or synchronous IPC wait on realtime callback. Native worker failure results in bounded bypass/silence defined by domain policy and recoverable diagnostics; committed edits remain durable.

WIT inputs use bounded chunk/handle protocols where copying arbitrary lists would amplify memory. Component Store/resource counts and retained artifacts receive explicit maxima. Reject shared memory/threads and unsupported imports unless separately budgeted and proven. Keep execution-engine choice replaceable behind the domain interface; benchmark wasmi compatibility lane before replacing it with Wasmtime.

rejected_approaches.approach: Universal native Rust dylib trait-object interface
rejected_approaches.reason: Rust ABI offers no stability guarantee; same-build trait abstraction is not independently versioned ABI.

rejected_approaches.approach: Declare existing Photo/Effect v1 artifacts WIT components
rejected_approaches.reason: Inspected exports implement distinct core-Wasm ABIs; migration requires an explicit adapter and independent ABI tests.

rejected_approaches.approach: Wasm sandbox plus fuel means hard realtime or total resource containment
rejected_approaches.reason: Hostcalls, compilation, allocator/host scratch, reclamation, shared memory and aggregate instances need distinct controls.

rejected_approaches.approach: Run untrusted native scanner/process in application and rely on panic catching
rejected_approaches.reason: Native faults and hangs cross Rust unwind safety; load-time execution is also a fault boundary.

rejected_approaches.approach: Global upstream plugin registry or per-domain platform catalog/DB/scheduler
rejected_approaches.reason: Account isolation and shared platform ownership cannot be supplied by process-global registration or duplicate owners.

primary_sources.claim: Native Rust ABI no stability guarantees; explicit external ABI is separate.
WIT worlds imports/exports and owned/borrowed resources define interfaces; they do not authorize resources or guarantee realtime behavior.
Guest access depends on host imports; host policy remains part of security.
Store lifetime retains instances; resource limits and execution interruption are separate controls.
ResourceLimiter does not account all runtime/embedder memory or CPU; shared-memory growth is a limitation; explicitly set resource counts rather than defaults.
Component API distinct from core modules; WIT bindgen generated host traits/types and gated features.
Fuel deterministic with overhead; epoch interruption nondeterministic; trapping and yielding have different semantics.
Init/destroy/activate/deactivate main-thread; start/stop/process audio-thread with state constraints.
Component/controller persistence sequencing, configuration/activation/processing lifecycle and main/audio threading requirements.

DIFF_ATTACK_SURFACES: No product diff authorized; attack surfaces derive from proposed adoption compared directly with pinned source
INDEPENDENT_CHECKS_RUN: Direct source call-chain review from CPAL callback to CLAP state FFI against official state.h
Direct VST3 capture/restore result-path inspection against official persistence sequence
Photo/Effect import, memory/fuel, pooling and registry inspection
Exact local source SHA256 reconciliation and Cargo.lock wasmi2.0.0 resolution
Tagged Wasmtime resource-limiter/component source inspected independently of latest documentation
COUNTERFACTUAL_CHECKS: If Photo runtime module.imports rejection were removed, empty linker alone would no longer express the intended closed-capability policy for a future adapter that adds imports.
If Effect take/give retained guest instances without principal binding in a multi-account host, previous guest state could affect later principals and replay.
If VST load_state ignored controller restore rejection, a document could report restored while processor/controller states disagree.
If CLAP state save remained inside playback fill, moving DB writes off the callback would still leave the main-thread ABI mismatch.

BOUNDARY_PROBES.boundary: audio caller versus CLAP state callee
Wasm Store limit versus host aggregate
core-Wasm exports versus WIT component interfaces

future_proof_plan.proof: Independent CLAP/VST thread-checking plugins and official validators; instrument lifecycle affinity and forbidden callback allocation/state calls; original-host save/load roundtrip with artifact identity and parameter/audio equivalence. Measure supported device block sizes and callback tails; do not invent passed SLOs.

Hostile native load/init/process/state/destroy crashes and hangs in isolated worker; verify UI liveness, bounded bypass deadline, quarantine, clean restart and no lost accepted edits. Independent process/resource oracle needed; static FFI review cannot prove isolation.

Multi-language WIT components exercise owned/borrowed resources, version mismatch, malformed handles, revocation during invocation, undeclared imports, large buffers, nested hostcalls, infinite guest loops and hostcall cancellation. Measure CPU/RSS/allocator/instance peaks across concurrent principals including compiled artifacts and teardown.

Fresh versus pooled/reordered guest invocation and cross-principal sentinel tests; assert no private state/log/source-path leakage and deterministic domain result where promised. Leak checks cover failure, cancel, shutdown, restart and rejected proposals.

Plugin state absent/truncated/oversized/version-mismatched/controller-refused with fault injection before/after accepted transaction. Independent DB re-read proves edit/state/receipt atomicity, stale conflicts and idempotent retries bound to principal/resource/content/expected revision; standalone EventLedger append is insufficient.

Saturation/starvation/deadlock/drain proof across preview/export/realtime and cancellation; compare worst-case RSS/bytes/instance/device limits with admissions; verify permits retained through retirement, all terminal paths reclaim once, cancel lane available, accepted edits durable. Thresholds must be specified before execution.

RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: No upstream plugin/runtime execution, build, native GUI, fault injection or audio measurement performed.
Wasmtime stable49.0.2 tagged source is a research reference; dependency/platform compatibility and security release selection require fresh implementation-time review.
Current official documentation links are mutable; tagged sources are version references, not cryptographic commit attestations until accompanying fetched-byte hashes are verified.
Process isolation, hostcall cancellation and realtime transport are proposed controls requiring external runtime oracles.
Complete shared platform catalog/library/grant implementation was not established by inspected source; preserve planned-gap status.
